description: References as they are parsed from a text. Server and client parse the same text in different languages; a reference the phone shows as a chip and the server does not write to the table is worse than no reference at all.
note: The normalized form is expected: 'key:<KEY>' for the typed form #TD-14, 'uri:<TYPE>/<uuid>' for the form from the link picker. In the order of the text and without duplicates -- both sides then resolve to the same row of the link table. The type is upper case, the address lower case: hiwiski://wiki_page/... becomes WIKI_PAGE.

cases.name: the typed form
cases.why: The convenient case. Assumes the number has already been assigned.

cases.name: the form from the picker
cases.why: The reliable form. It also works for an item that was created offline and has no number yet -- which is exactly why the picker always inserts it.

cases.name: both forms in one text, in the order of the text
cases.why: They end up in the same table. The order is that of the text, not that of the notations -- otherwise the UI would show the chips differently from how they appear in the text.

cases.name: the same reference twice yields one row
cases.why: The table has a unique index on it. A duplicate entry would be an error on writing instead of on reading.

cases.name: a bare address without Markdown brackets
cases.why: Whoever types it by hand or copies it from the address bar means the same reference.

cases.name: a heading is not a reference
cases.why: Markdown uses the same character. Between '# Einkauf' and '#TD-14' there is a space, and that is what decides it.

cases.name: lower case is not a key
cases.why: The readable key is upper case -- '#td-14' is text that someone meant that way.

cases.name: a number without digits is not a reference
cases.why: '#TD-' is a beginning, not a key. Half a match would be worse than none.

cases.name: a broken address yields no reference
cases.why: A UUID that is too short is not a user error worth pointing out -- it simply yields no reference.

cases.name: a key inside a link label is not a reference
cases.why: The label is display text. The server used to find the #TD-14 in it as well, the device did not -- backlinks and the offline info bar disagreed.

cases.name: a label with escaped brackets
cases.why: The picker escapes brackets in a title. Ending the label at the first ] broke the link apart.

cases.name: an unclosed bracket does not hide what follows it
cases.why: Both sides skip the brackets that cannot start a link, so that a line of them is read in linear time. Skipping must not lose the bare address, the key or the next link after the line break.

cases.name: an open bracket before a link belongs to its label
cases.why: The label runs from the first bracket to the closing one, as it always did -- a bracket inside it is text.

cases.name: empty text
cases.why: A task without a description is the normal case and must not be treated differently from one with.
